section_heading: 1.1 What is built, in what order; the two size ladders
text: **The village product's one registration** (SS-19; reconciliation round 1). **Consolidated.** The one registration is `ProductDecl` in `StrategyRegistry.products: Map<'base'|'village', ProductDecl>` (V07 §2.1's type; BCR-V7-11); `LadderRouter.route` reads it — a registered product's rung for a population inside that product's range, the base's clamp otherwise. The port asks `LadderRouter` whether a population lies in a registered product's range, at `creation` and at every `absorb`, and registers nothing itself: BCR-V8-9's `PortRungPath` and `registerRungPath` are dropped (withdrawn into this item). §1.1 *Requests at the ends of the ladder*: the routing sentence names the registration ("… to the village product registered in `StrategyRegistry.products` (§4.12; PART III)"); the refusal of a dossier below 1 500 (there and in §7.7 item 15) holds only while no village product is registered; with one registered, an absorb whose population is 0 routes to THORP and runs volume 7's desertion (V07 §3.12; an outcome, not a refusal), while a creation below 1 stays refused (BCR-V7-17); the product at an epoch is item 322's fold (§4.11). §1.1's sentence "A dossier's rung follows its population by these bands, at creation and at each epoch's target (§4.11), while its own tier word titles the map (§9.5)." reads "A dossier's rung follows its population by these bands at creation and, at each epoch's target, by §4.11's rung at an epoch (inside the hand-off band item 322 brings to §4.11 from volume 7 §2.1, the previous product's edge row), while its own tier word titles the map (§9.5)." (SR1-29; reconciliation round 2). §4.12: BCR-V7-11's pipeline-order sentence as written. PART III gains one line: "the product registers its `ProductDecl` in `StrategyRegistry.products` (§4.12); the port consults `LadderRouter` at creation and at every absorb; one document crosses the 1 500 boundary by item 322's fold"; and in PART III's last paragraph "waits for the village product's own port path, which registers its rung rows behind the same port (§14) rather than a second one" reads "waits for the village product's registration (its `ProductDecl`, §4.12), which the one port consults through `LadderRouter`" (SR1-29; reconciliation round 2). **The records hook** (seam-time-r5 TW-03 (3), seam-settlements-r5 SR5-15 (a); reconciliation round 6): `ProductDecl.records?` (V07 §2.1; an `EpochPlacement`, V6 §2.1, with its placement and, for a removed record, its removal) and its calls as BCR-V7-18 words them are hooks of this registration — at an epoch whose product (item 322's fold) declares it, the dossier step's (§4.11's order (e)) for each `assign` it places — a record it adds, a member a count step adds, or the greater a REPLACEMENT re-key places new (V08 §3.5.1 (c)'s second and third cases, (d)); a re-key whose greater keeps the lesser's thing is a `rebind`, never offered (seam-time-r6 TX-06) — and for the records it removes; and for an absorb without an epoch at a rung of that product, the placement of each record it adds and the removal call after each it removes — and so are, before volume 6 lands, the product's two phase overrides (`siting`, `growth`), which `grow-by-stage` consults, and its participants — all at **the call points** this item adds to the grow path's order in §4.11 (a)–(j), at the places V6 §3.2's table gives the same steps, so volume 6's runner reproduces them (T-V6-1): the `siting` override in place of step (f)'s placement and the `growth` override in place of step (g)'s; the records placement's `place` inside step (e) before each added record's *One path* placement and its `remove` after each §7.7 item 2 removal; the participants registered at `afterField` after step (a) and before (b), at `decline` at the end of (c), and at `afterGrowth` after (g) and before (h), each in (order, id) order, each run's ops one batch of the `epoch` event. They are called with volume 6's `ProductEpochContext` (V6 §2.1: doc, epoch, seq, week, prevWeek, years, inputs, tables, product, rung, productRows?, stream(stage, entity), scope()), which the grow path fills and which lands with this item beside `EpochPhase`, `EpochParticipant`, `EpochPlacement` and `ProductDeclEpoch`; the placement takes the five-member pick (doc, tables, product, rung, week) an absorb fills; volume 6's `EpochContext` extends it at M6-E (seam-time-r6 TX-02; finalization). Volume 4's own M4 hooks stay BCR-6's sentences at their fixed places. They land with this registration on M4's grow path (V07 §8's V-M2 row; TW-03 (1), (2)), and BCR-V6-1 (a) carries them into its phase interface at M6-E (item 317). The absorb-path placement call is inserted in §7.7's *One path — placement, then mutation* sentence "every `assign` event … is placed by §4.7 S10b's one solver for its scope": at a rung of a product that declares `ProductDecl.records`, an added record is first offered to that placement, which places it or declines it, and a declined record takes S10b's placement as that sentence gives it. The requests' "§7.7 item 2's placement" means this sentence; §7.7's item 2 is *Existence* and places nothing, and its removal of a record (through `closeUse`) is what the removal call follows. *Requests:* BCR-V7-11, BCR-V8-9, BCR-V7-17, BCR-V7-18 (its `records` member and calls, and its grow-path overrides and participants; its phases in the phase interface with item 317). Also touches: §4.11 (the dossier step's call; the grow path's call points), §4.12, §7.7, PART III. *Needed by:* V06, V07, V08. **STAGED (the village product, V-M0 to V-M4; the port's consultation with the SettlementForge stage, SF0 to SF7).**

text: **The raised-way record** (g item 110 (b), homed by the coherence pass) — one record for all volumes. **Consolidated (J-VI.2, J-VI.15, J-VI.21).** A raised way is a `Way` (§2.4) on a ground arena part ≥ 1 whose `Way` record gains `raised?: RaisedWayRecord`, declared in §2.7: `{ kind: 'viaduct'|'elevated'|'aqueduct'; reason?: RaisedReasonKey /* generated ways; volume 6 §2.13; the reason WORD shown by readers and exports is derived: viaduct → 'drop', elevated → 'link', aqueduct → 'water' */; underuseSince?: number /* volume 6 */; supports: { key: number; ring: Polygon; state?: 'ruined'|'cleared' }[]; spans: { a: number; b: number; use: 'open'|'vault'; reason: 'way'|'water'|'flood'|'tall'|'low'|'slope'|'chance'|'cap'|'land'|'user'; soffitCm: Cm /* derived */; held?: true; state?: 'ruined'|'cleared' }[]; terminal?: { kind: 'basin'|'cistern'|'fountain'; at: PointCm; building?: Id }; feeds?: Id[]; waterUse?: Id; clearanceCm?: Cm /* held once a user edits it (BCR-V9-33); absent: derived, below */; spanSpacingCm?: Cm /* held once edited (BCR-V9-33); absent: drawn, below */ }`. **The support step** (J-VI.27; integration continuation, 2026-09-29), run for every raised way — generated, declared or drawn — after its course and deck level are fixed and before the span rule, from ground part 0 only: (1) the deck's centre-line between its two feet (where its ramps or stairs meet part 0) has length L m; the pitch p is `spanSpacingCm` ÷ 100 where held, else one uniform on the raised-way stream keyed by (the way's lineage, `pitch`) inside the `pierSpacingM` band of the way's material (volume 11's `raisedWays.structure`, the material drawn by its `material` row by band; an aqueduct never timber); (2) n = max(1, round(L ÷ p)) spans, the n − 1 interior stations evenly spaced at L ÷ n; (3) a station whose pier would meet a part-0 way's corridor or a water face slides along the deck to the nearest clear position at which both neighbouring spans stay ≤ `raisedWays.structure.slideMaxFactor` × the band's upper bound (1.5; volume 11's cell, row 80; own, calibrate-later, `extension`; seam SCC-114), else it is omitted and the merged span is `open` by the span rule's step (2); (4) each pier's `ring` is a rectangle centred on its station, across the deck of the deck's width and along it of max(`pierWidthShare` × the realised span, `pierMinCm` ÷ 100) m; a pier higher than `maxPierM[kind]` (the deck's level less `levelledGroundCm` at its station) drops a generated course (`raised_too_tall`, volume 11) and makes a declared one's dry run bend it to the nearest course the pier heights admit (item 101 R2; rule R-a); (5) keys are minted in order along the deck and never reused (V04 BCR-45): an unchanged course re-derives the same stations from the same stream key and so keeps its keys; a changed course keeps the key of every station within p ÷ 2 of a former one and mints the rest after the largest key the way has held. **The clearance:** over each crossed part-0 way the deck stands at least `clearanceCm` + `raised.deckDepthCm` above that way's levelled ground, `clearanceCm` the held value or, absent, volume 11's `raisedWays.structure.clearanceCm` for the crossed class (cart or foot); the course solver reads it as the deck's lower bound there (volume 11: the cells bound the deck's level, never set it), and a held value below the crossed class's is bent up to it (`bend.raised.clearance`, BCR-V9-33). The piers the step lays are read by volume 1's crossings and under-deck strip, volume 4's arch vaults and foundations, volume 5's access siting, volume 6's decay and clearance, volume 7's obstacles, volume 9's **Deck height** and **Arch spacing** steppers and the exports (item 447). Sources of the fields: BCR-V9-33 (`clearanceCm`, `spanSpacingCm`; the support step, J-VI.27), V04 BCR-45 (supports, spans and **the span rule**, terminal, feeds, `raised.deckDepthCm` 150 and `raised.supportFoundationCm` 400), BCR-V6-25 (b) (reason key, `underuseSince`, the span and support `state`), BCR-V8-28 (`waterUse`), J-VI.2 as amended by ST-06 (the derived source and word), J-VI.9 (`terminal.kind` `cistern` only under a conduit house the roster or dossier holds). A raised way's **source** is derived at read, never stored (ST-06; reconciliation round 1): `declared` when the way's lifecycle cause is an edit or a skeleton file, else `generated` (volume 6 §3.19.1 (2)); there is no `carried` value — a reader that says "carried down from year N" reads the lifecycle and the epochs' rungs (volume 6 §4.5) — and no stored founding rung (the founding epoch's `EpochRecord` holds it). Lifecycle: generated ways re-derive with their reason key; declared ways are held; a removal of a generated way is a suppression (the suppression item); undo is the log's; migration: absent `raised` is a ground way. The **II.7.6 Vaults** sentence is V04 BCR-45's. *Requests:* V04 BCR-45, BCR-V8-28, BCR-V9-33. *Needed by:* V01, V04, V05, V06, V07, V08, V09, V11. **BASE (M3a (the record, the support step and the span rule); the arch-vault chambers M6-U).**

text: **The `RetainingWall` record** (g item 110 (a)) — one record for all volumes. **Consolidated.** `RetainingWall { id; chain: ChainRef /* on the ground layer, or on a sky island's arena (BCR-V5-27) */; highSide: 'left'|'right' /* resolved at the dry run when drawn without it (BCR-V9-26 (a)); generated: the side D holds (V01 BCR-42) */; closed: boolean /* a platform, high side inside (BCR-V9-26 (a)) */; material: string /* volume 11's MaterialRow key (BCR-V11-30) */; buttresses?: …; towers?: … /* decorative, a table row */; source: 'generated'|'declared'; state?: RetainingState | ChainProfile<RetainingState> /* 'retaining_state_knot' on the chain, step (§2.2 rule 5, J-K10): the wall's condition by stretch; a constant state is a scalar; absent = 'standing' throughout (TR-14) */ }` with `type RetainingState = 'standing'|'decayed'|'ruined'`; the step profile is a **derived view** `stepProfile(wall)` never stored (V01 BCR-43). §2.2 rule 7's knot roles gain `retaining_state_knot` (indexed, as every knot role). Never an `Enceinte`; no gate, no circuit, no barrier closure. Lifecycle as item 110 (a) states, and for `state`: **The state profile** (TR-14; reconciliation round 2). *Writers:* BCR-V6-26's retaining member (`breach` → `decayed`, `dismantle` → `ruined`), `repairRetaining` (a `decayed` run back to `standing`; volume 6 §2.8, item 209) and volume 5's landfall (`decayed` over its covered length, V5 §3.16 (4)); volume 7's house-platform walls decay through volume 6's pool (V07 §3.12). Each writes over its `StretchRef` — the whole chain when it names none — by a knot at each end, an end that is no vertex placed first by `splitThrough` (§3.4): the near knot carries the new state, the far knot the state that held there before; since a step profile is constant before its first knot (§2.2 rule 5), an open wall's profile always keeps a knot on the chain's first vertex (placed with the value that held there when a scalar is first expanded), a closed wall's needs none. The writer then drops every knot whose value equals the knot before it (never an open chain's first-vertex knot), stores a profile whose values are all equal as that scalar, and a scalar `standing` as absent — one canonical form, so the digest (§6.3) is stable. *Read* by `sampleProfile` by arc length (§3.4; a closed wall's profile cyclic): the pool and the restoration rule (volume 6 §3.19.4), volume 4's footings (a footing stands where the wall stands), the renderer (each run drawn by its state row, BCR-V6-26's §8.2 rows), item 447's export and the clerk. *Persisted* as the knot rows and values. *Regenerated:* a generated wall re-derived where an epoch levels keeps its profile while it is not restored (volume 6 §3.19.4 (1), (6)): a knot stays on its vertex while the vertex survives (carry-over by lattice point, §3.10, §6.3); a knot whose vertex is gone is re-placed by `splitThrough` at the new chain's point nearest its old point when that point lies within `retaining.settings.stateSnapCm` (volume 11's `retaining` table, its named `settings` row; 100 cm; our own, calibrate-later; seam SCC-114), else dropped and its run merged into the run before it (an open wall's first-vertex knot always re-placed on the new chain's first vertex); the restoration writes `standing` over the re-levelled length. A cut or join of the chain carries the profile by J-K23's `rekey` pairing. *Undo:* the writing op's undo record restores the former profile, knot rows included. *Migrate:* absent reads `standing`; a document holding the pre-round-2 scalar reads it as the constant profile. *Requests:* V01 BCR-43, BCR-V5-27; the state profile TR-14 (integration). *Needed by:* V01, V04, V05, V06, V07, V09. **BASE (M3a; the island form M6-sky; the state profile's writers with their ops — M6-E, M6-sky).**
